subject: rw14b elevated 5xx & timeouts — initial notice and recovery update
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-08T09:04:12Z
Subject: rw14b: Elevated 5xx and timeouts observed — heads up

Team,

Monitoring is flagging an increase in 5xx responses and client-side timeouts for the rw14b model starting ~2026-05-08T08:58Z. Spike characteristics:
- Error type: internal 5xx (kernel OOM / RPC timeouts) and gateway timeouts (504)
- Affected traffic: ~6% of total rw14b inference requests across hosted API region us-west1
- Error TTL: spikes in 1-3 minute bursts over the past 10 minutes

Attached: rw14b-5xx-sample-logs.txt (sample request IDs and stack traces), grafana-rw14b-error-panel.png (error rate panels).

Preliminary findings: a nightly kernel upgrade (quantization kernel update) was deployed to a small subset of hosts for rw14b at 2026-05-08T02:20Z; canary looked stable under our synthetic tests but we've hit higher-than-expected failure rates for sequences >1024 tokens in production.

Mitigation options we can push now:
1) Route affected customers on rw14b to rw11b fallback for 30-60m (preserves availability, slightly different quality profile).
2) Roll back the kernel change on canary hosts and escalate rollout hold.
3) Apply an automated retry at the gateway for specific transient RPC errors (short-term).

Recommend we notify affected customers (Acme.ai appears impacted) with a brief note that we are investigating and to request any client-side blocked request IDs so we can correlate. Also recommend offering to route Acme to rw11b while we investigate.

I'll follow with additional logs and a short timeline.

— Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>, Acme AI Support <support@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-08T09:18:37Z
Subject: Re: rw14b elevated 5xx & timeouts — initial notice and recovery update

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the heads up, and apologies for the disruption. We’ve detected elevated 5xx and timeout errors for requests routed to our rw14b model since ~08:58 UTC. Immediate summary:

- Impact: intermittent 5xx / 504s for a subset of requests (roughly 6% of rw14b traffic). You may see errors or slow responses for some calls to your routed model.
- Short-term action taken by Redwood: we have either (a) started routing your rw14b traffic to our rw11b fallback, or (b) can implement this within minutes if you prefer. This preserves availability while we investigate quality differences. Please confirm if you want us to switch your production route now; otherwise we will proactively route to rw11b for affected requests.
- What we’re investigating: a recent quantization/kernel change appears correlated with failures on long-sequence requests (>1024 tokens). We are rolling back the kernel change on canary hosts and evaluating a full rollback if we reproduce the issue.
- Ask from you: if you can share any failed request IDs (example: req_abc123), timestamps, or sample inputs that failed, that will help correlation.

Status updates: we’ll send a next update within 30 minutes and a recovery confirmation once traffic has normalized. We’ll also follow up with a postmortem and offer credits if SLAs were affected.

Attachments: Incident-summary-05-08.pdf (brief snapshot for your records).

Apologies again for the disruption — we’re prioritizing this and will keep you closely informed.

Best,

Sofia Ivanova
Senior Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0123

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme AI Support <support@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-08T09:25:04Z
Subject: Re: rw14b elevated 5xx & timeouts — initial notice and recovery update

Thanks Sofia — we started seeing errors at ~08:59 UTC. Example request id: req_20260508_ACME_41f7. The errors have impacted parts of our chat flow for end-users (timeouts on assistant replies).

Two quick asks:
1) Please route our rw14b traffic to the fallback (rw11b) immediately — we need availability over parity.
2) Can you confirm whether this is expected to trigger any pricing or SLA adjustments? We have renewals coming up and want to understand impact.

Appreciate the quick response.

— Daniel Park
Head of AI Engineering, Acme.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-08T10:05:33Z
Subject: rw14b incident recovery and next steps (May 8)

Hi Daniel —

Quick recovery update and planned follow-ups:

Timeline (UTC):
- 08:58 — Monitoring alert: rw14b 5xx spike begins.
- 09:04 — Internal triage (SRE) identifies kernel/quantization change correlation.
- 09:18 — Customer notice sent (Sofia).
- 09:22 — We routed Acme.ai traffic to rw11b fallback (completed).
- 09:35 — Rollback of kernel change initiated on canary hosts.
- 09:42 — Error rate returned to baseline for rw14b; observing stable traffic.

Root cause (preliminary): a quantization kernel update introduced regression for long-sequence workloads (>1024 tokens) on a subset of inference hosts, causing increased kernel memory pressure and RPC timeouts. The change had passed synthetic canary tests but failed to capture specific production sequence distributions.

Remediations completed:
- Immediate rollback on canary hosts and hold of full rollout.
- Customer traffic routed to rw11b while we validated rollback and recovery.
- Automated alerts adjusted to detect sequence-length correlated failure patterns.

Next steps:
- We will run an expanded validation matrix (long-sequence, multi-batch) and publish a postmortem by 2026-05-12.
- Offer: we’ll apply a one-time service credit (10% of May usage for impacted routes) and schedule a review meeting — suggested slot: 2026-05-10 15:00 UTC. Please let us know if that works.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-05-08.md (internal draft), rw14b-5xx-sample-logs.txt.

If you have any more request ids or dates/times of end-user impact, forward them and we’ll correlate. Thanks for your patience — we’ll follow up with the formal postmortem and mitigation plan.

Best regards,

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0199
